frozen_decisions: Stage 2 uses one logical agent by default
Stage 3 is the first controlled single versus isolated-workers execution ablation boundary
Stage 4 independent producer, verifier, and critic separation is a later work package
Stage 5 and Stage 7 remain deterministic code, while Stage 6 remains one semantic evaluator plus deterministic scheduling in the first release
The isolated-workers hypothesis is limited to bounded parallelism, context isolation, independent counter-review, and task-level failure isolation; it does not claim intrinsic intelligence
Both execution modes share the same frozen scope, source snapshot, model family, prompt family, configured budgets, schemas, scoring contract, validators, and final domain contract
Both modes receive a forbidden-field-clean counter packet; the single shared-session arm reports context_blind=false, while an isolated critic must prove a distinct worker identity and fresh context
Mode-independent task_key and execution-specific task_id are separate identities; task_key excludes run, pair, mode, execution, worker, attempt, and actual-usage identity
Proof-eligible Phase A and Phase B pairs use a pre-sealed strict-replay task plan; divergent dynamic shadow plans cannot support topology-only causal claims
Ablation and shadow arms persist execution-scoped candidate results and cannot mutate canonical Stage 3 state or RunStatus without an explicit authorized promotion
The default production mode remains single until the documented gates pass
Mastra, LangGraph, and a lightweight Python executor remain unselected until framework-neutral contracts and Phase A evidence exist
